The structure of CsMg14Bi crystallizes in the tetragonal space group I-4m2 (No. 119), with a 32-atom unit cell (Cs2Mg28Bi2) and five independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived coordination analysis shows Bi and Cs centers each surrounded by 16 neighbors, while Mg centers adopt 12-neighbor close-packed-like local arrangements. Mg polyhedra share corners, edges, and faces with one another and with Bi- and Cs-centered polyhedra, forming a three-dimensional connected network.
